entities.summary:
Khankendi, known historically to Armenians as Stepanakert, stands as a pivotal urban center in the Nagorno-Karabakh region, a territory whose contested status has ignited multiple conflicts between Azerbaijan and Armenia. Its strategic location in the Lesser Caucasus mountains, coupled with its demographic history, rendered it the de facto capital of the self-proclaimed Artsakh Republic from 1991 until Azerbaijan reasserted full control in 2023. This city embodies centuries of complex ethnic coexistence, imperial shifts, and modern nationalistic aspirations, making it a microcosm of the broader geopolitical struggles in the South Caucasus.

Originally a small Armenian village called Vararakn, it was significantly developed into Stepanakert during the Soviet era, becoming the administrative center of the Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast (NKAO) in 1923, named after Armenian Bolshevik leader Stepan Shaumian. Throughout the 20th century, the city experienced substantial population growth and industrialization, attracting both Armenians and Azerbaijanis, though Armenians constituted the dominant majority. The late 1980s saw the city become a focal point for the Karabakh movement, leading to the First Nagorno-Karabakh War (1988-1994), during which it suffered extensive damage from shelling and siege, yet remained under Armenian control. Following the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh War and the Azerbaijani offensive in September 2023, the city's Armenian population, estimated at nearly 50,000, largely departed, fundamentally altering its demographic and political landscape.
